<reason>B won the live comparison: both sides conceded rising distrust and euro survival, but A kept collapsing solidarity into retained membership while B made that metric look thin, nearly unfalsifiable, and at odds with democratic overrides, creditor-bank protection, lasting party-system damage, and the architects’ own refusal to repeat the playbook. A’s political-constraint and different-shock replies were real, yet they never showed why those cheques outweighed the residue B described.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s pressure-to-closing sequence: force a fail-condition for “everyone stayed,” then map 2015 Greece and the pandemic redesign onto A’s own internment/cheques test and treat the new fund as participants’ verdict on the old method.</best_rebuttal>
